The plan stage stays exactly as it was. A fourth movement sits between the usage read and the catalogue, because the argument only works in that order: here is your plan, here is what you have actually been doing with it, therefore here is where that sits and what is either side.

Three rungs, current in the middle, `<ol>` with `aria-current` on the here rung. A hairline runs through the three nodes so it reads as a ladder rather than a row of price cards. The current rung is the only one on `--bg` with a brand border and a filled node; the neighbours sit back on `--bg-secondary`. Nothing on a rung is clickable. No price, no currency symbol, no Start button anywhere: I probed the section's innerText for `[$£€]|per month|/mo|GST|NZD` and the only hit was the phrase "a monthly read on the site".

The rule that carries the whole section, and the thing I would most like Liam to sign off:

**A rung only carries a number if the number is the client's own.**

Scale prints "2 tracks, building at the same time" and "6.4 days from asked to delivered, averaged over your own work", both real. Maintain and Launch are described entirely in words. That is forced by the product (per the reader map, only maintain and scale have a rate, a Stripe product, catalogue copy or a track entitlement; tune, launch, hourly and custom are labels and dropdown options), but it also happens to be the thing that stops three cards in a row reading as a pricing table, which is exactly what "no prices pressure" is guarding against. Each rung carries a one line "Best if…" and three rows: Tracks, Turnaround, Included.

Ladder order is `tune, maintain, scale, launch`, which is the order the brief listed them in. Hourly is deliberately not a rung: it is named in a plain note under the ladder, "Two kinds of work sit off this ladder entirely: small jobs billed by the hour, and one off projects scoped and quoted on their own." A custom plan resolves to no ladder at all rather than being stood on a row of steps it is not on. A Tune client sees two rungs, a Launch client sees two; the grid handles `data-n="2"`.

THE UPSELL
Absent, not disabled, until usage earns it. `D.planPressure()` returns signals and the card renders only if the array is non-empty. Three signals, the ones named in the brief:

- queue: fires when `queued > tracks`. I moved this one notch off the brief. "Queue depth at the track count" would fire at 2 waiting with 2 tracks, but at exactly the track count everything already has somewhere to go the moment a track frees. The edge starts one past it. With the demo data (4 waiting, 2 tracks) it fires and reads "There are 4 things waiting and 2 tracks to pull them onto. Even when both free up, 2 of them keep waiting." Say the word and I will move it back to `>=`.
- tracks: fires at 85 percent of available track days. 7 of 8 in September, so it fires.
- hours: implemented, and returns nothing for a retainer client because there is no cap to be near. The previous designer's "no hours on this page" decision stands; this signal exists for the hourly plan it was written for, and the resolver refuses to invent a denominator.

The card is warm, brand tinted, one action ("Talk about moving up", opening the existing AskSheet seeded with "About moving from Scale to Launch: " and the standard "Nothing changes on your bill from here" line). Every sentence in it is the consequence of a number the page has already printed above it. It closes with "Plenty of clients sit here on purpose and never move, and this is a suggestion rather than a push to spend more." When nothing fires, a calm strip says so out loud rather than leaving a hole: "Nothing in your numbers says you are pushing against Scale at the moment, so there is nothing here you need to move to."
